newsitem.title: JORDAN: Germany approves $60 million aid package to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Germany approves $60 million aid package to Jordan.

text.p: Germany signed on Thursday with Jordan a new aid package for 1997 whose major portion is earmarked to help the kingdom ease poverty, officials said.

They said the protocol, signed in talks in Amman between senior Jordanian and German economic officials, involves a total package of 102 million marks ($60 million) in technical assistance, grants, soft loans and debt forgiveness.

The actual financial commitments are 50 million marks, 10 percent higher than 1996, which include 30 million marks in soft loans and another 20 million marks of grants to buttress social projects under an ambitious Jordanian plan unveiled last week to tackle poverty.

The soft loans will finance the renovation of the water system in the capital Amman, and the second largest city of Irbid and promote studies for projects to tap more water resources in joint Israeli-Jordanian projects charted in a 1994 peace treaty.

Germany, which helped build many of the kingdom's water and irrigation projects, has pledged to play a role in financing ambitious multi-million dollar water projects between Jordan and Israel to cement Middle East peace.
A further 12 million marks are in the form of technical assistance in water, customs, agriculture, and transportation areas.

Under the accord, Germany also committed itself to write off up to 40 million marks of Jordanian debt provided the kingdom transforms an equivalent sum it now pays to Bonn in annual interest on its debt into projects under its social safety net plan.
It follows a similar scheme agreed in 1995 under which Jordan was given a sum of 79.5 million marks in a debt swap deal tied to undertaking projects.

Jordan, a major importer of German goods, has received a total of 1.43 billion marks in soft loans and grants since Bonn started its assistance programme in the early 1960s. -- Amman Newsroom +9626-623776
